## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)

No multi-country ADR is accepted yet, so this section is **logical**. The physical modelling
(content types, components, how the country is attached, the API IDs) is decided by the
multi-country ADR and implemented by the strapi-developer following `strapi-content-modeling`.

### 7.1 Field configuration (per country, draft & publish on)

| Attribute | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | Required. `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$`. Unique per country. Not shown to users. |
| `label` | string | Required, non-empty. Spanish. |
| `type` | enumeration | `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`. |
| `isRequired` | boolean | Default `false`. |
| `helpText` | text | Optional. Spanish. |
| `placeholder` | string | Optional. Spanish. Never used instead of a label. |
| `errorMessage` | string | Required. Spanish. Field-level message (US-01-Q-04). |
| `sortOrder` | integer | Required. Ascending; ties by `key`. |
| `options` | list of { `value` string, `label` string, `sortOrder` integer } | Required and non-empty when `type` is `select`; ignored otherwise. `value` unique within the field. |
| `rules` | list of structured rules (below) | Zero or more, in evaluation order. Each may carry an optional `message` (Spanish) that overrides `errorMessage`. |
| `requiredMessage` | string | Optional. Overrides `errorMessage` for the `required` check. |
| country | per multi-country ADR | Exactly one country per field. |

Rule kinds (structured, not free JSON):

| Kind | Parameters | Applies to | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minLength` / `maxLength` | `value` integer ≥ 0 | text | Trimmed length, inclusive. |
| `min` / `max` | `value` number | number | Inclusive. |
| `pattern` | `value` ECMAScript regex source, no flags | text | Full match (anchored if not anchored). |
| `minAge` | `years` integer > 0 | date | BR-04. |
| `yearRange` | `maxYearsOld` integer ≥ 0, `maxYearsAhead` integer ≥ 0 | number | BR-03. |
| `rutCheckDigit` | none | text | Modulo-11 check digit, accepts dots/dash and `K`/`k` (subject to US-01-Q-09). |

A rule whose kind does not apply to the field's type is malformed (US-01-Q-18).

### 7.2 Seed (US-01-Q-03): summary

The complete seed (rules, help texts, error messages, options) is in the annex
[seed-fields.md](seed-fields.md). Values are fictitious, copy is Spanish, and every entry is
published unless noted. The seed is idempotent (natural key: country code + field `key`).

Fields per country, in `sortOrder` (key → label):

| # | Colombia (CO), 10 published | Chile (CL), 9 published |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `documentType` → Tipo de documento (select: CC, CE) | `documentNumber` → RUT (pattern + `rutCheckDigit`) |
| 2 | `documentNumber` → Número de documento | `fullName` → Nombre completo |
| 3 | `fullName` → Nombre completo | `birthDate` → Fecha de nacimiento (`minAge` 18) |
| 4 | `birthDate` → Fecha de nacimiento (`minAge` 18) | `city` → Ciudad (select) |
| 5 | `city` → Ciudad (select) | `plate` → Patente |
| 6 | `plate` → Placa | `make` → Marca (select) |
| 7 | `make` → Marca (select) | `model` → Modelo |
| 8 | `model` → Línea | `vehicleYear` → Año (`yearRange` 20 / 1) |
| 9 | `vehicleYear` → Modelo (año) (`yearRange` 20 / 1) | `dataConsent` → Acepto el tratamiento de mis datos personales. (checkbox) |
| 10 | `dataConsent` → Autorizo el tratamiento de mis datos personales. (checkbox) | — |
| draft | `email` → Correo electrónico (draft only, AC-13) | `email` → Correo electrónico (draft only) |

Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08, §7.3): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
`birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.


### 7.3 Step 1 output (consumed by US-02 and US-03 through the wizard state)

- `country`: `'CO' | 'CL'`.
- `values`: a map from field `key` to value. `text` → trimmed string; `number` → integer;
  `select` → option `value`; `date` → ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string; `checkbox` → boolean. An empty
  optional field → `null`.
- The field configuration used to render the step (labels and option labels), so later steps can
  display values without refetching or hard-coding labels. Whether it is stored or refetched is a
  persistence ADR detail.
- Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
  `birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.

### 7.4 Differences from the `dynamic-form-fields` skill contract v0

The skill says the US-01 spec may refine the contract and that the skill is updated in the same
PR. Differences proposed here:

1. A required field-level `errorMessage` plus optional per-rule overrides (`requiredMessage`,
   rule `message`), instead of only a per-rule-kind `messages` map (US-01-Q-04).
2. A new rule kind `rutCheckDigit` (US-01-Q-09).
3. `number` fields are integers only (US-01-Q-12).
4. Empty optional fields skip all rules (US-01-Q-26). The skill does not state this.
5. Rules carry an applicability by field type (§7.1); a mismatch is malformed.

## 8. UI states

| State | Trigger | What the user sees | Accessibility notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loading | Country resolved, configuration request in flight | Step heading and "Cargando formulario…"; no fields, no "Continuar" | Container has `aria-busy="true"`; the loading text is in a polite live region |
| Unsupported country | Missing or unsupported country (US-01-Q-01) | "Este país no está disponible." and links "Colombia", "Chile" | Message is the page's main heading; links are reachable by Tab |
| Error | Timeout (10 s), network or HTTP error, or zero valid fields | "No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de nuevo." and "Reintentar" | Message in `role="alert"`; focus moves to "Reintentar" |
| Partial content | Some fields malformed | The valid fields only; nothing extra is shown to the user | Console warning only (no user data) |
| Ready (pristine) | Configuration loaded | Fields in sortOrder, help texts, required marker note, "Continuar" | Label bound to every control; help text in `aria-describedby`; required exposed |
| Field invalid | Blur or failed "Continuar" | Configured message right below the field | `aria-invalid="true"`; error in `aria-describedby`; announced once |
| Failed continue | "Continuar" with invalid fields | All errors shown; step does not change | Focus on the first invalid field in sortOrder |
| Success | "Continuar" with a valid form | The address changes to the step 2 route; its page is US-02's (no page of its own in US-01, US-01-Q-27) | Focus on the step 2 heading and document title: defined and verified in US-02 |
| Back to step 1 | Browser back (and "Atrás" on step 2, once US-02 exists) | Step 1 with the stored values, no errors | Focus on the step 1 heading |

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- **Accessibility (Assessment):** the step can be completed with the keyboard only (AC-24), and
  every field has an accessible label (AC-25). Native controls are used (`input` of type text,
  number, date and checkbox; `select`). Visible focus indicator. Errors are associated with their
  field and announced once. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for step 1 (verified in part automatically and in
  part by hand at HC3, including one screen reader pass).
- **Responsive (Assessment):** usable from 320 to 1440 CSS px wide without horizontal scroll;
  verified by hand at HC3 at 360 × 740 and 1280 × 800, with screenshots as evidence (AC-26); one
  column; touch targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px.
- **Multi-country (Assessment):** one build for CO and CL; no country-specific code paths for
  fields or copy (BR-07).
- **Content-driven (Assessment, BR-06):** every field-related string, option, rule and the order
  come from Strapi. No field list is hard-coded in the front end.
- **Typed validations (Assessment):** the configuration is parsed at the boundary into a typed
  model (§7.1) before it reaches the form; validators are pure functions with an injectable clock.
- **Security / privacy (Assessment, CLAUDE.md §3):** no Strapi token with write permissions
  reaches the browser; the browser only reads content (AC-27). Public role permissions are
  minimal and justified in the security ADR. Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written
  to logs; console warnings contain no user data. Seed and test data are fictitious.
- **Performance:** the configuration of a country is loaded with as few requests as the content
  model allows (target: one), with options and rules populated in the same response. No request
  per keystroke. Validation runs on the client.
- **Environment (Assessment):** the stack starts with a single command (for example
  `docker compose up`) with the seed for both countries.
- **Language:** all end-user copy is Spanish; code, logs and docs are English.

## 10. ADRs

- **Referenced (accepted):** none yet.
- **Needed (for the architect):**
  1. **Multi-country content strategy:** the Strapi model for country-specific fields (options
     A–D in `strapi-content-modeling`), where country metadata lives, and how Angular resolves
     the country context, including the root address, unsupported countries and switching.
     Inputs: BR-07, US-01-Q-01, US-01-Q-02, §7. Shared with US-02 and US-03.
  2. **Forms library (SPIKE-01):** Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms for a form built at runtime
     from §7.1. Beyond the cases already listed in CLAUDE.md §7 (required number, empty date,
     select, legal age), the spike should also cover: hydrating the form from the wizard state
     (AC-04), dropping stored values for removed fields (AC-23), error display timing and focusing
     the first invalid field (AC-10), and integer-only numbers (AC-05). This spec is
     library-agnostic.
  3. **Strapi access and security model:** public role (`find` only) vs. a read-only token
     behind a server-side proxy; runtime configuration of the API URL so the same build serves
     every environment; no caching that breaks BR-06 (US-01-Q-16); how e2e tests write test
     content without exposing write tokens to the browser (US-01-Q-23). Inputs: AC-27, AC-03.
  4. **Front-end persistence of wizard state:** in-memory vs `sessionStorage` vs `localStorage`;
     what is stored (personal data included), scoping per country, and when it is cleared
     (country switch, tab close, after payment in US-03). Inputs: BR-08, US-01-Q-02,
     US-01-Q-15, AC-04, AC-20, AC-21, AC-22.
  - Candidate for the architect to fold into ADR 1 or write separately: **wizard routing and
    step guards** (step URLs, history entries per step, guard rule of US-01-Q-19, focus
    management on step change). Shared by all three stories. Since v0.2 it also covers how the
    step 2 route exists before its page (US-01-Q-27).

If the route does not exist, a valid "Continuar" fails or falls into the not-found handling, and those checks cannot pass. | US-01 registers the step 2 route of each country (address per the routing decision, §10) with the AC-19 guard and **no page of its own**: no heading, no copy, no buttons. US-02 attaches its page to that route without changing the address or the guard. Until then, a valid "Continuar" changes the address to step 2 and shows an empty content area (the browser back action returns to step 1 with its data); tests assert the address, not page content. Alternative: US-01 registers no step 2 route; the e2e tests of AC-24 and AC-27 stop at activating "Continuar" with a valid form, and the AC-19 guard is merged without a route. | Proposed default accepted: US-01 registers each country's step 2 route with the AC-19 guard and no page of its own; US-02 attaches its page to that route without changing the address or the guard; tests assert the address. — Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20 (HC1 round 2) |
609	
610	Checklist items with no gap: *double clicks / submits* — step 1 sends nothing to a server, and a
611	second activation of "Continuar" while on step 2 has no effect. *Currency and number
612	formatting* — no amounts in step 1 (US-02). *Masking* — no masking in step 1, where the user is
613	typing their own data (US-03 masks the summary).
614	
615	## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)
616	
617	No multi-country ADR is accepted yet, so this section is **logical**. The physical modelling
618	(content types, components, how the country is attached, the API IDs) is decided by the
619	multi-country ADR and implemented by the strapi-developer following `strapi-content-modeling`.
620	
621	### 7.1 Field configuration (per country, draft & publish on)
622	
623	| Attribute | Type | Rules |
624	|---|---|---|
625	| `key` | string | Required. `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$`. Unique per country. Not shown to users. |
626	| `label` | string | Required, non-empty. Spanish. |
627	| `type` | enumeration | `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`. |
628	| `isRequired` | boolean | Default `false`. |
629	| `helpText` | text | Optional. Spanish. |
630	| `placeholder` | string | Optional. Spanish. Never used instead of a label. |
631	| `errorMessage` | string | Required. Spanish. Field-level message (US-01-Q-04). |
632	| `sortOrder` | integer | Required. Ascending; ties by `key`. |
633	| `options` | list of { `value` string, `label` string, `sortOrder` integer } | Required and non-empty when `type` is `select`; ignored otherwise. `value` unique within the field. |
634	| `rules` | list of structured rules (below) | Zero or more, in evaluation order. Each may carry an optional `message` (Spanish) that overrides `errorMessage`. |
635	| `requiredMessage` | string | Optional. Overrides `errorMessage` for the `required` check. |
636	| country | per multi-country ADR | Exactly one country per field. |
637	
638	Rule kinds (structured, not free JSON):
639	
640	| Kind | Parameters | Applies to | Semantics |
641	|---|---|---|---|
642	| `minLength` / `maxLength` | `value` integer ≥ 0 | text | Trimmed length, inclusive. |
643	| `min` / `max` | `value` number | number | Inclusive. |
644	| `pattern` | `value` ECMAScript regex source, no flags | text | Full match (anchored if not anchored). |
645	| `minAge` | `years` integer > 0 | date | BR-04. |
646	| `yearRange` | `maxYearsOld` integer ≥ 0, `maxYearsAhead` integer ≥ 0 | number | BR-03. |
647	| `rutCheckDigit` | none | text | Modulo-11 check digit, accepts dots/dash and `K`/`k` (subject to US-01-Q-09). |
648	
649	A rule whose kind does not apply to the field's type is malformed (US-01-Q-18).
650	
651	### 7.2 Seed (US-01-Q-03): summary
652	
653	The complete seed (rules, help texts, error messages, options) is in the annex
654	[seed-fields.md](seed-fields.md). Values are fictitious, copy is Spanish, and every entry is
655	published unless noted. The seed is idempotent (natural key: country code + field `key`).
656	
657	Fields per country, in `sortOrder` (key → label):
658	
659	| # | Colombia (CO), 10 published | Chile (CL), 9 published |
660	|---|---|---|
661	| 1 | `documentType` → Tipo de documento (select: CC, CE) | `documentNumber` → RUT (pattern + `rutCheckDigit`) |
662	| 2 | `documentNumber` → Número de documento | `fullName` → Nombre completo |
663	| 3 | `fullName` → Nombre completo | `birthDate` → Fecha de nacimiento (`minAge` 18) |
664	| 4 | `birthDate` → Fecha de nacimiento (`minAge` 18) | `city` → Ciudad (select) |
665	| 5 | `city` → Ciudad (select) | `plate` → Patente |
666	| 6 | `plate` → Placa | `make` → Marca (select) |
667	| 7 | `make` → Marca (select) | `model` → Modelo |
668	| 8 | `model` → Línea | `vehicleYear` → Año (`yearRange` 20 / 1) |
669	| 9 | `vehicleYear` → Modelo (año) (`yearRange` 20 / 1) | `dataConsent` → Acepto el tratamiento de mis datos personales. (checkbox) |
670	| 10 | `dataConsent` → Autorizo el tratamiento de mis datos personales. (checkbox) | — |
671	| draft | `email` → Correo electrónico (draft only, AC-13) | `email` → Correo electrónico (draft only) |
672	
673	Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08, §7.3): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
674	`birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.
675	
676	
677	### 7.3 Step 1 output (consumed by US-02 and US-03 through the wizard state)
678	
679	- `country`: `'CO' | 'CL'`.
680	- `values`: a map from field `key` to value. `text` → trimmed string; `number` → integer;
681	  `select` → option `value`; `date` → ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string; `checkbox` → boolean. An empty
682	  optional field → `null`.
683	- The field configuration used to render the step (labels and option labels), so later steps can
684	  display values without refetching or hard-coding labels. Whether it is stored or refetched is a
685	  persistence ADR detail.
686	- Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
687	  `birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.
688	
689	### 7.4 Differences from the `dynamic-form-fields` skill contract v0
690	
691	The skill says the US-01 spec may refine the contract and that the skill is updated in the same
692	PR. Differences proposed here:
693	
694	1. A required field-level `errorMessage` plus optional per-rule overrides (`requiredMessage`,
695	   rule `message`), instead of only a per-rule-kind `messages` map (US-01-Q-04).
696	2. A new rule kind `rutCheckDigit` (US-01-Q-09).
697	3. `number` fields are integers only (US-01-Q-12).
698	4. Empty optional fields skip all rules (US-01-Q-26). The skill does not state this.
699	5. Rules carry an applicability by field type (§7.1); a mismatch is malformed.
700	
701	## 8. UI states
702	
703	| State | Trigger | What the user sees | Accessibility notes |
704	|---|---|---|---|
705	| Loading | Country resolved, configuration request in flight | Step heading and "Cargando formulario…"; no fields, no "Continuar" | Container has `aria-busy="true"`; the loading text is in a polite live region |
706	| Unsupported country | Missing or unsupported country (US-01-Q-01) | "Este país no está disponible." and links "Colombia", "Chile" | Message is the page's main heading; links are reachable by Tab |
707	| Error | Timeout (10 s), network or HTTP error, or zero valid fields | "No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de nuevo." and "Reintentar" | Message in `role="alert"`; focus moves to "Reintentar" |
708	| Partial content | Some fields malformed | The valid fields only; nothing extra is shown to the user | Console warning only (no user data) |
709	| Ready (pristine) | Configuration loaded | Fields in sortOrder, help texts, required marker note, "Continuar" | Label bound to every control; help text in `aria-describedby`; required exposed |
710	| Field invalid | Blur or failed "Continuar" | Configured message right below the field | `aria-invalid="true"`; error in `aria-describedby`; announced once |
711	| Failed continue | "Continuar" with invalid fields | All errors shown; step does not change | Focus on the first invalid field in sortOrder |
712	| Success | "Continuar" with a valid form | The address changes to the step 2 route; its page is US-02's (no page of its own in US-01, US-01-Q-27) | Focus on the step 2 heading and document title: defined and verified in US-02 |
713	| Back to step 1 | Browser back (and "Atrás" on step 2, once US-02 exists) | Step 1 with the stored values, no errors | Focus on the step 1 heading |
714	
715	## 9. Non-functional requirements
716	
717	- **Accessibility (Assessment):** the step can be completed with the keyboard only (AC-24), and
718	  every field has an accessible label (AC-25). Native controls are used (`input` of type text,
719	  number, date and checkbox; `select`). Visible focus indicator. Errors are associated with their
720	  field and announced once. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for step 1 (verified in part automatically and in
721	  part by hand at HC3, including one screen reader pass).
722	- **Responsive (Assessment):** usable from 320 to 1440 CSS px wide without horizontal scroll;
723	  verified by hand at HC3 at 360 × 740 and 1280 × 800, with screenshots as evidence (AC-26); one
724	  column; touch targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px.
725	- **Multi-country (Assessment):** one build for CO and CL; no country-specific code paths for
726	  fields or copy (BR-07).
727	- **Content-driven (Assessment, BR-06):** every field-related string, option, rule and the order
728	  come from Strapi. No field list is hard-coded in the front end.
729	- **Typed validations (Assessment):** the configuration is parsed at the boundary into a typed
730	  model (§7.1) before it reaches the form; validators are pure functions with an injectable clock.
731	- **Security / privacy (Assessment, CLAUDE.md §3):** no Strapi token with write permissions
732	  reaches the browser; the browser only reads content (AC-27). Public role permissions are
733	  minimal and justified in the security ADR. Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written
734	  to logs; console warnings contain no user data. Seed and test data are fictitious.
735	- **Performance:** the configuration of a country is loaded with as few requests as the content
736	  model allows (target: one), with options and rules populated in the same response. No request
737	  per keystroke. Validation runs on the client.
738	- **Environment (Assessment):** the stack starts with a single command (for example
739	  `docker compose up`) with the seed for both countries.
740	- **Language:** all end-user copy is Spanish; code, logs and docs are English.
741	
742	## 10. ADRs
743	
744	- **Referenced (accepted):** none yet.
745	- **Needed (for the architect):**
746	  1. **Multi-country content strategy:** the Strapi model for country-specific fields (options
747	     A–D in `strapi-content-modeling`), where country metadata lives, and how Angular resolves
748	     the country context, including the root address, unsupported countries and switching.
749	     Inputs: BR-07, US-01-Q-01, US-01-Q-02, §7. Shared with US-02 and US-03.
750	  2. **Forms library (SPIKE-01):** Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms for a form built at runtime
751	     from §7.1. Beyond the cases already listed in CLAUDE.md §7 (required number, empty date,
752	     select, legal age), the spike should also cover: hydrating the form from the wizard state
753	     (AC-04), dropping stored values for removed fields (AC-23), error display timing and focusing
754	     the first invalid field (AC-10), and integer-only numbers (AC-05). This spec is
755	     library-agnostic.
756	  3. **Strapi access and security model:** public role (`find` only) vs. a read-only token
757	     behind a server-side proxy; runtime configuration of the API URL so the same build serves
758	     every environment; no caching that breaks BR-06 (US-01-Q-16); how e2e tests write test
759	     content without exposing write tokens to the browser (US-01-Q-23). Inputs: AC-27, AC-03.
760	  4. **Front-end persistence of wizard state:** in-memory vs `sessionStorage` vs `localStorage`;
761	     what is stored (personal data included), scoping per country, and when it is cleared
762	     (country switch, tab close, after payment in US-03). Inputs: BR-08, US-01-Q-02,
763	     US-01-Q-15, AC-04, AC-20, AC-21, AC-22.
764	  - Candidate for the architect to fold into ADR 1 or write separately: **wizard routing and
765	    step guards** (step URLs, history entries per step, guard rule of US-01-Q-19, focus
766	    management on step change). Shared by all three stories. Since v0.2 it also covers how the
767	    step 2 route exists before its page (US-01-Q-27).

# CLAUDE.md

Global context for every agent working in this repository (main session and subagents).
The rules here are binding. If a rule seems wrong, stop and ask the human; do not work around it.

Related files: [FLOW.md](FLOW.md) (the flow, step by step), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (catalogue of
agents and skills), [README.md](README.md) (how to run the project).

## 1. Precedence of instructions

An explicit instruction from the human in the session overrides everything below, and it must be
**recorded** where it applies (spec Review log, ADR, or `tasks.md`) so the decision is traceable.
Among the written sources, when two disagree, the higher one wins:

1. **`CLAUDE.md`** (this file)
2. **Accepted ADRs** in `adr/` (status `Accepted`; `Proposed` ADRs are not binding)
3. **Project skills**: skills in `.claude/skills/` written for this project
4. **Third-party skills**: vendored skills listed in `.claude/skills/THIRD_PARTY.md`

A third-party skill never overrides a project decision. If one tells you to do something that a
higher source forbids or has not yet decided, follow the higher source and note the conflict in
your output.

## 2. Language

- Everything in the repository is in **English**: code, identifiers, comments, Markdown docs
  (README, FLOW, specs, ADRs, reviews), commit messages, branch names, PRs, review comments,
  and agent and skill definitions.
- **End-user content is in Spanish**: Strapi seed data (labels, help texts, error messages,
  plans, coverages, terms and conditions), because the users are in Colombia and Chile.

## 3. Security and data

- Never print tokens, secrets or the contents of `.env` files in any output.
- `.env` is git-ignored. Only `.env.example` with fictitious values is committed.
- Only fictitious data anywhere in the repo (people, documents, plates, cards).
- No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser.
- Do not use skills, plugins or memory from the user's global `~/.claude`. Everything the flow
  uses is versioned in this repository.

## 4. Toolchain versions (pinned)

| Tool | Version | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Angular CLI / framework | **22.3.0** (latest stable, verified on npm on 2026-11-20) | Scaffold with `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new …`. **Never use `@latest`** or an unpinned `npx @angular/cli`. Pin exact versions in `package.json` (no `^`/`~` on `@angular/*`). |
| Unit tests | Vitest (Angular 22 CLI default) | — |
| E2E tests | `@playwright/test` | Do not use `playwright-ng-schematics` unless a human approves it. |

Upgrading any pinned version requires an ADR or an explicit human approval recorded in the
relevant `tasks.md`.

## 5. Third-party skill overrides

These rules override the vendored `angular-developer` skill (see
`docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`, EVAL-001):

- **Forms strategy is not taken from the skill.** `references/signal-forms.md` says Signal Forms
  are mandatory. Ignore that: Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms is decided by an ADR after
  SPIKE-01 (see §7). Until that ADR is accepted, do not write production form code.
- **The Angular CLI MCP server is not used.** Do not configure it (`references/mcp.md`) and do
  not run `npx @angular/cli mcp`.
- **The Angular CLI version is pinned** (§4). The skill's "no version / `@latest`" defaults do
  not apply.
- **Naming follows §6**, not the skill's ambiguous examples.
- **Keyboard accessibility of the wizard** is enforced by the project `review-checklist` skill.
  The skill's ARIA guidance is supplementary.
- Reads of `angular.dev` are allowed as a reference, but any decision based on them must be
  written into a spec or ADR.
- Never edit vendored skill files. Overrides go here.

## 6. Naming conventions

Status: **Accepted** — approved by Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20.

The rule is to follow the Angular 22 CLI defaults (no role suffix in file or class names)
and to use **intent-revealing names** so the role stays obvious without a suffix.

### Angular (`frontend/`)

| Artifact | File | Identifier | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Component | `kebab-case.ts` + `.html` + `.css` (same base name) | `PascalCase`, no `Component` suffix | `plan-list.ts` → `PlanList` |
| Routed page (wizard step) | `<step>-page.ts` | `…Page` | `quote-form-page.ts` → `QuoteFormPage` |
| Service: HTTP access | `<domain>-api.ts` | `…Api` | `country-content-api.ts` → `CountryContentApi` |
| Service: signal state | `<domain>-store.ts` | `…Store` | `quote-store.ts` → `QuoteStore` |
| Guard / interceptor / resolver (functions) | `<name>-guard.ts`, `-interceptor.ts`, `-resolver.ts` | `camelCase` + role | `wizard-step-guard.ts` → `wizardStepGuard` |
| Pipe | `<name>-pipe.ts` | `…Pipe`; template name `camelCase` | `masked-document-pipe.ts` → `MaskedDocumentPipe` / `maskedDocument` |
| Directive | `<name>.ts` | `PascalCase` | `autofocus-error.ts` → `AutofocusError` |
| Types / models | `<domain>.model.ts` | `PascalCase` interfaces and types, no `I` prefix | `field-config.model.ts` → `FieldConfig` |
| Pure functions | `<domain>.ts` | `camelCase` exported functions | `price-rules.ts` → `calculateFinalPrice()` |
| Validators | `<domain>-validators.ts` | `camelCase` factories | `field-validators.ts` → `legalAge()` |
| Unit tests | `<same-base-name>.spec.ts` next to the file | `describe('<US-AC id> …')` | `price-rules.spec.ts` |
| E2E tests | `frontend/e2e/<us-ids>-<slug>.spec.ts` | `test('<US-AC id> …')` | `us-01-03-full-flow-co.spec.ts` |
| Component selector prefix | — | `app-` | `app-plan-card` |
| Constants and injection tokens | in the file that owns them | `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` | `STRAPI_BASE_URL` |

Folders: `src/app/core/` (singletons, API clients, interceptors), `src/app/features/<feature>/`
(wizard steps), `src/app/shared/` (reusable presentational UI, pipes, pure functions).

### Strapi (`backend/`)

- Content-type API IDs: singular `kebab-case` (`form-field`, `plan`, `country`, `terms`).
- Components: `category.kebab-name` (`form.select-option`, `plan.coverage`).
- Attribute names: `camelCase` (`isRecommended`, `sortOrder`, `errorMessage`).
- Custom code files: `kebab-case.ts`.

### Repository artifacts

- Specs: `specs/US-01/{story,spec,tasks}.md`
- ADRs: `adr/NNNN-kebab-title.md` (4-digit, sequential)
- Reviews: `reviews/US-01-review-R1.md`
- Branches: `feat/us-01-short-slug`, `fix/us-01-…`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`

## 7. Pending decisions

| ID | Decision | How it will be resolved | Blocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPIKE-01 | **Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms** for the Strapi-driven step 1 form | Throwaway spike on a `spike/01-forms` branch that is never merged, run by the frontend-developer. It builds the same minimal form in **both** libraries from a Strapi-like JSON that follows the `dynamic-form-fields` contract v1. Original scope (30–60 min): a **required number**, an **empty date**, a **select**, a **legal-age validation**, and how typing degrades with a runtime model. Added at HC1 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): **hydrating** the form from stored values; **dropping** values of fields no longer configured; **when errors appear** (touched / submit attempt); **focus on the first invalid field**; **integer-only** numbers; mapping empty optional fields to **`null` in the step 1 output** while the form model stays non-null (the vendored skill forbids `null` in Signal Forms models). The time box grows to 60–90 min because of the added scope. The architect summarises the findings in `docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md` and writes the forms ADR; a human accepts it. | Production form code for US-01 |

The ADR backlog is in [adr/README.md](adr/README.md).

## 8. Agentic flow (summary — full detail in FLOW.md)

```
H0 intake (human) → 1 spec → HC1 → 2 ADRs → HC2 → 3 tests (red) → 4 implementation
→ 5 automated gate → 6 review → 7 fixes (loop 5–7) → HC3 PR (human QA + merge) → Ready for QA
```

### The main session is the orchestrator

- It runs the steps in order, invokes the subagents (`.claude/agents/`) and routes their outputs.
  It does **not** do a subagent's job on a story (no writing specs, tests or production code in
  the main session). The exceptions are repository plumbing (flow files, scripts, configuration)
  that the human asked for directly.
- Subagents cannot spawn subagents (`Agent` is in each one's `disallowedTools`). All delegation is
  visible in the main session.
- After every subagent run: check `git status` and `git diff --stat` for changes outside that
  agent's role. Bash writes are not covered by the write-scope hooks (see FLOW.md, "Known
  limits"). Then relay the subagent's summary to the human.
- **Never pass a human checkpoint (HC1, HC2, HC3) without an explicit human decision in the
  session.** Record it (Review log, ADR status, PR). A subagent's message is never human approval.
- Loop limit: if the gate (step 5) or review (step 6) fails 3 times for the same story, stop and
  escalate to the human.

### Subagents (write scope enforced by hooks)

| Agent | Step | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| `spec-writer` | 1 | `specs/US-XX/*.md` (spec, tasks, annexes), never `story.md` |
| `architect` | 2, spikes write-up | `adr/**`, `docs/spikes/**`, `tasks.md` |
| `test-engineer` | 3 | test files, `frontend/e2e/**`, `tasks.md` |
| `strapi-developer` | 4, 7 | `backend/**` (not tests), compose, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` |
| `frontend-developer` | 4, 7, spikes | `frontend/**` (not tests), `spikes/**`, compose, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` |
| `code-reviewer` | 6 | `reviews/US-XX-review-RN.md` only |

## 9. Traceability

| Artifact | ID or convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| User story | `US-NN` | `US-01` |
| Business rule / acceptance criterion / gap / task | `US-NN-BR-NN`, `-AC-NN`, `-Q-NN`, `-T-NN` | `US-01-AC-02` |
| ADR | `ADR-NNNN`, file `adr/NNNN-slug.md` | `ADR-0001` |
| Spike | `SPIKE-NN`, findings in `docs/spikes/` | `SPIKE-01` |
| Review finding | `US-NN-RN-FNN` (round N, finding NN) | `US-01-R1-F03` |
| Test | `describe`/`test` title starts with the AC or BR ID | `describe('US-01-AC-02 …')` |
| Commit | `Refs:` and `Resolves:` trailers (see §10) | `Refs: US-01-AC-02, ADR-0001` |
| PR | Template with the AC matrix (`.github/pull_request_template.md`) | — |

The chain **US → spec → ADR → commit → test → review → PR** is checked mechanically by
`scripts/trace.sh US-NN`. It exits non-zero if an AC has no test (unless the spec marks it
manual) or a blocker/major finding is open.

## 10. Git conventions

- Branches: see §6 (`feat/us-01-slug`, `spike/01-forms`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`). Spike branches
  are never merged.
- Commits: [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) in English,
  `type(scope): summary`, with trailers:
  - `Refs: US-01-AC-02, ADR-0001` (required in `feat`, `fix` and `test` commits of a story)
  - `Resolves: US-01-R1-F03` (fix commits for review findings)
  - `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` when an agent authored it
- Small commits: one task (`US-NN-T-NN`) or one finding per commit where practical. Tests and
  production code go in separate commits (they come from different agents).
- Local identity only (`git config --local`). The author is the human; agents are co-authors.
- No pushes to `main`, no force pushes, and no `--no-verify` (enforced by
  `.claude/hooks/guard-bash.mjs`). Changes reach `main` only through a PR merged by the human.

## 11. Session continuity

Follow the `session-handoff` skill at the start and end of every session. The state of each story
lives in `specs/US-NN/tasks.md` (*Current step*, *Next action*). Session logs are exported,
unedited, to `logs/sessions/`.

## 12. Definition of Done (Ready for QA)

A story is **Ready for QA** when all of these hold:

- [ ] The spec is `Approved` (HC1), and the ADRs it needs are `Accepted` (HC2).
- [ ] Every AC is implemented and has a passing automated test, or a documented manual check.
- [ ] Lint, build, unit and e2e pass. `docker compose up` starts the stack with seed data for CO and CL.

- ➖ The model shape is only known at runtime, so typing degrades to `Record<string, …>`.

# CLAUDE.md

Global context for every agent working in this repository (main session and subagents).
The rules here are binding. If a rule seems wrong, stop and ask the human; do not work around it.

Related files: [FLOW.md](FLOW.md) (the flow, step by step), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (catalogue of
agents and skills), [README.md](README.md) (how to run the project).

## 1. Precedence of instructions

An explicit instruction from the human in the session overrides everything below, and it must be
**recorded** where it applies (spec Review log, ADR, or `tasks.md`) so the decision is traceable.
Among the written sources, when two disagree, the higher one wins:

1. **`CLAUDE.md`** (this file)
2. **Accepted ADRs** in `adr/` (status `Accepted`; `Proposed` ADRs are not binding)
3. **Project skills**: skills in `.claude/skills/` written for this project
4. **Third-party skills**: vendored skills listed in `.claude/skills/THIRD_PARTY.md`

A third-party skill never overrides a project decision. If one tells you to do something that a
higher source forbids or has not yet decided, follow the higher source and note the conflict in
your output.

## 2. Language

- Everything in the repository is in **English**: code, identifiers, comments, Markdown docs
  (README, FLOW, specs, ADRs, reviews), commit messages, branch names, PRs, review comments,
  and agent and skill definitions.
- **End-user content is in Spanish**: Strapi seed data (labels, help texts, error messages,
  plans, coverages, terms and conditions), because the users are in Colombia and Chile.

## 3. Security and data

- Never print tokens, secrets or the contents of `.env` files in any output.
- `.env` is git-ignored. Only `.env.example` with fictitious values is committed.
- Only fictitious data anywhere in the repo (people, documents, plates, cards).
- No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser.
- Do not use skills, plugins or memory from the user's global `~/.claude`. Everything the flow
  uses is versioned in this repository.

## 4. Toolchain versions (pinned)

| Tool | Version | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Angular CLI / framework | **22.3.0** (latest stable, verified on npm on 2026-11-20) | Scaffold with `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new …`. **Never use `@latest`** or an unpinned `npx @angular/cli`. Pin exact versions in `package.json` (no `^`/`~` on `@angular/*`). |
| Unit tests | Vitest (Angular 22 CLI default) | — |
| E2E tests | `@playwright/test` | Do not use `playwright-ng-schematics` unless a human approves it. |

Upgrading any pinned version requires an ADR or an explicit human approval recorded in the
relevant `tasks.md`.

## 5. Third-party skill overrides

These rules override the vendored `angular-developer` skill (see
`docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`, EVAL-001):

- **Forms strategy is not taken from the skill.** `references/signal-forms.md` says Signal Forms
  are mandatory. Ignore that: Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms is decided by an ADR after
  SPIKE-01 (see §7). Until that ADR is accepted, do not write production form code.
- **The Angular CLI MCP server is not used.** Do not configure it (`references/mcp.md`) and do
  not run `npx @angular/cli mcp`.
- **The Angular CLI version is pinned** (§4). The skill's "no version / `@latest`" defaults do
  not apply.
- **Naming follows §6**, not the skill's ambiguous examples.
- **Keyboard accessibility of the wizard** is enforced by the project `review-checklist` skill.
  The skill's ARIA guidance is supplementary.
- Reads of `angular.dev` are allowed as a reference, but any decision based on them must be
  written into a spec or ADR.
- Never edit vendored skill files. Overrides go here.

## 6. Naming conventions

Status: **Accepted** — approved by Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20.

The rule is to follow the Angular 22 CLI defaults (no role suffix in file or class names)
and to use **intent-revealing names** so the role stays obvious without a suffix.

### Angular (`frontend/`)

| Artifact | File | Identifier | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Component | `kebab-case.ts` + `.html` + `.css` (same base name) | `PascalCase`, no `Component` suffix | `plan-list.ts` → `PlanList` |
| Routed page (wizard step) | `<step>-page.ts` | `…Page` | `quote-form-page.ts` → `QuoteFormPage` |
| Service: HTTP access | `<domain>-api.ts` | `…Api` | `country-content-api.ts` → `CountryContentApi` |
| Service: signal state | `<domain>-store.ts` | `…Store` | `quote-store.ts` → `QuoteStore` |
| Guard / interceptor / resolver (functions) | `<name>-guard.ts`, `-interceptor.ts`, `-resolver.ts` | `camelCase` + role | `wizard-step-guard.ts` → `wizardStepGuard` |
| Pipe | `<name>-pipe.ts` | `…Pipe`; template name `camelCase` | `masked-document-pipe.ts` → `MaskedDocumentPipe` / `maskedDocument` |
| Directive | `<name>.ts` | `PascalCase` | `autofocus-error.ts` → `AutofocusError` |
| Types / models | `<domain>.model.ts` | `PascalCase` interfaces and types, no `I` prefix | `field-config.model.ts` → `FieldConfig` |
| Pure functions | `<domain>.ts` | `camelCase` exported functions | `price-rules.ts` → `calculateFinalPrice()` |
| Validators | `<domain>-validators.ts` | `camelCase` factories | `field-validators.ts` → `legalAge()` |
| Unit tests | `<same-base-name>.spec.ts` next to the file | `describe('<US-AC id> …')` | `price-rules.spec.ts` |

| Component selector prefix | — | `app-` | `app-plan-card` |
| Constants and injection tokens | in the file that owns them | `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` | `STRAPI_BASE_URL` |

Folders: `src/app/core/` (singletons, API clients, interceptors), `src/app/features/<feature>/`
(wizard steps), `src/app/shared/` (reusable presentational UI, pipes, pure functions).

## 8. Agentic flow (summary — full detail in FLOW.md)

```

→ 5 automated gate → 6 review → 7 fixes (loop 5–7) → HC3 PR (human QA + merge) → Ready for QA

| User story | `US-NN` | `US-01` |

  `.claude/hooks/guard-bash.mjs`). Changes reach `main` only through a PR merged by the human.

## 11. Session continuity

Follow the `session-handoff` skill at the start and end of every session. The state of each story
lives in `specs/US-NN/tasks.md` (*Current step*, *Next action*). Session logs are exported,
unedited, to `logs/sessions/`.

## 12. Definition of Done (Ready for QA)

A story is **Ready for QA** when all of these hold:

- [ ] The spec is `Approved` (HC1), and the ADRs it needs are `Accepted` (HC2).
- [ ] Every AC is implemented and has a passing automated test, or a documented manual check.
- [ ] Lint, build, unit and e2e pass. `docker compose up` starts the stack with seed data for CO and CL.
- [ ] `scripts/trace.sh US-NN` exits 0, and `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` exits 0.
- [ ] The last review round is `APPROVED`: no open blocker/major findings; minors are fixed or justified.
- [ ] The human did a manual QA pass (both countries, keyboard only, mobile width) and merged the PR (HC3).
- [ ] `tasks.md` shows `Ready for QA`, and the session logs are exported.

# Third-party skill evaluations

Every external skill is evaluated **before** installation. Each one is read from its
source repository (not from a registry summary) and checked against the project

Only a human can approve an installation. Approved skills are recorded in
`.claude/skills/THIRD_PARTY.md`.

Verdict scale: **ADOPT** · **ADOPT WITH ADJUSTMENTS** · **REJECT**.

### Criteria reviewed

#### 1. Compatibility with project requirements

Latest stable Angular at evaluation time: **22.3.0** (npm `latest`; `next` = 22.3.0-rc.0).
The assessment requires Angular 21 or later, so 22.x qualifies.

| Requirement | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Angular 21+ / latest stable | ✅ | Targets "latest versions"; tells the agent to detect the project's version first (SKILL.md rule 1). |
| Standalone, no NgModules | ✅ | `components.md`: standalone is the default since v19. `NgModule` appears only in the standalone migration guide and in `TestBed` explanations. |
| Signals | ✅ | `signal`, `computed`, `linkedSignal`, `resource`, `httpResource`, signal inputs, outputs and queries. |
| Built-in control flow `@if/@for` | ✅ | All templates use `@if/@for/@switch`; no `*ngIf/*ngFor` anywhere. |
| Vitest | ✅ | `testing-fundamentals.md` assumes Vitest, zoneless, and an "Act, Wait, Assert" pattern with `await fixture.whenStable()`. `cli.md` still mentions Karma as a possible runner (neutral). |
| Playwright | ⚠️ Neutral | `e2e-testing.md` lists 5 frameworks and suggests `ng add playwright-ng-schematics`, a community package, not an official Angular one. It does not conflict, but it brings no Playwright guidance of its own. |
| Keyboard accessibility | ⚠️ Partial | `angular-aria.md` covers keyboard interaction for complex widgets (listbox, combobox, tabs…). Nothing on wizard focus management, focus on errors or `aria-describedby` for field errors. Our `review-checklist` must still cover this. |

#### 2. Conflicts with our CLAUDE.md and own skills

| # | Rule in the skill | Conflict | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `signal-forms.md`: "You MUST use Angular's new Signal Forms API for all form-related functionality" and "Do NOT import FormControl, FormGroup…" | It decides the forms strategy before our ADR does, and it contradicts `SKILL.md`, which allows Reactive Forms for complex or existing forms. | Precedence rule in `CLAUDE.md`: **CLAUDE.md > accepted ADRs > own skills > third-party skills**. The forms ADR decides. |
| C2 | SKILL.md rule 2 / `ng new`: "do not specify a version unless prompted"; falls back to `npx @angular/cli@latest` | Non-reproducible scaffolding. | `CLAUDE.md` pins the CLI version (`npx @angular/cli@22.3.x`). The skill's own Step 1 honours an explicit version. |
| C3 | `mcp.md`: configure the Angular CLI MCP server via `npx -y @angular/cli mcp` | User rule: no external tools; all context lives in the repo. | `CLAUDE.md`: do not configure MCP servers. The file stays unmodified so provenance is preserved, but it is not followed. |
| C4 | SKILL.md: "read the documentation at angular.dev" when the references are not enough | Remote reads; the context should live in the repo. | Read-only reads of `angular.dev` are allowed, but any decision based on them must be written into a spec or ADR. |
| C5 | `naming-conventions.md`: v20+ suffixless naming ("Intent over Role"), but also "respect existing project conventions"; its own examples are inconsistent (`auth.ts` → `class AuthService`) | Ambiguous until we decide. | `CLAUDE.md` states the naming convention explicitly (proposal: v22 CLI defaults, suffixless files). |
| C6 | `e2e-testing.md`: `ng add playwright-ng-schematics` | Pulls in a community dependency. | Playwright setup follows our `test-from-spec` skill (`@playwright/test` directly). The schematic is not used unless a human approves it. |
| C7 | SKILL.md rule 3: run `ng build` after generating code | None. It matches our automated gate. | Keep. |

No conflict with `sdd-spec`, `adr-madr`, `strapi-content-modeling` or `review-checklist`.
`dynamic-form-fields` and `test-from-spec` are **complementary** (see criterion 4).

#### 3. Security: commands, remote content, anything suspicious

- **No scripts, binaries or hooks.** Only Markdown files plus `BUILD_INFO`.
- Commands found: `ng build/test/e2e/add/generate`, `npx @angular/cli@<version> new`,
  `npx @angular/cli@latest new`, `npx -y @angular/cli mcp`. The `npx` calls download npm
  packages when executed; this is covered by C2 and C3.
- External domains: only `angular.dev` (docs), `api.example.com` (examples) and `localhost`.
- No hidden or bidirectional Unicode characters, no base64, no `curl | sh`, no instructions
  aimed at secrets, credentials or files outside the project.
- **Supply-chain note:** the content changes daily and `npx skills add` installs whatever
  is at HEAD, not the evaluated commit. Mitigation: after installation, diff the installed
  files against commit `97c663a`. If they differ, stop and re-evaluate.
- Licensing: MIT requires keeping the copyright notice. Because the mirror has no LICENSE
  file, `THIRD_PARTY.md` must record the notice and point to the upstream license.

#### 4. Value beyond our own skills and CLAUDE.md

| Area | Our coverage | What angular-developer adds |
|---|---|---|
| Signal Forms API (`form`, `[formField]`, `validate`, `applyEach`, `applyWhen`, `submit`, `validateStandardSchema`) | `dynamic-form-fields` covers the Strapi→validator **contract**, not the API | **High.** Up-to-date API reference with a "Common pitfalls" table and a section on recovering from build errors. This is where an LLM is most likely to hallucinate an API that only reached stable in v22. |
| Zoneless, async-first unit testing with Vitest | `test-from-spec` covers AC-ID naming and Gherkin→test mapping | **High.** Correct `whenStable()` patterns; avoids `detectChanges()` anti-patterns. |
| `resource` / `httpResource`, `linkedSignal`, `effect` guidance | Not covered | **Medium-high.** Loading and error states for Strapi calls (graded under "technical quality"). |
| Runtime configuration (`provideAppInitializer`) | Not covered | **Medium.** Relevant because the same build must serve CO and CL and point to Strapi at runtime. |
| Routing, guards, `@defer`, `@boundary` error boundaries | Not covered | **Medium.** Wizard step guards and error isolation. |
| SSR, Tailwind, animations, MCP, deployment | Not needed | None, but harmless because they load on demand. |

#### 5. Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms (input for the forms ADR)

**What the skill says**

- `SKILL.md`: "Use Signal Forms for form management in new projects (stable in Angular v22
  and newer)." Prefer Signal Forms for new forms on v22+. For older apps or existing forms,
  keep the current strategy. Reactive Forms are listed for "complex forms".
- `signal-forms.md`: Signal Forms are "the recommended approach… (v21+)". It **mandates**
  them for all forms and forbids `FormControl/FormGroup/FormBuilder`.
- This is an **internal inconsistency**: "v21+ / MUST" against "v22+ / prefer". We checked
  the official source instead of trusting either statement:

**Verified facts (latest stable 22.3.0)**

- `angular/angular` CHANGELOG, **22.0.0 (2026-06-03)**, forms: commit `7745365910`,
  *"graduate signal forms APIs to public API"*. In v21 they were experimental.
- Published `@angular/forms@22.3.0` typings: all `@angular/forms/signals` APIs are tagged
  `@publicApi 22.0` (one is `22.1`). The only `@experimental` symbol is
  `provideExperimentalWebMcpForms`, which we do not need.
- `@angular/forms/signals-compat` (`@publicApi 22.0`) provides `compatForm` and
  `SignalFormControl` to interoperate with Reactive Forms.
- The schema API we need is exported: `required`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `validate`,
  `applyEach`, `applyWhen`, `metadata`, `validateStandardSchema`, `submit`.

**Implications for a Strapi-driven dynamic form (to be weighed in the ADR)**

- ➕ The form structure is derived from a model signal, so a model built at runtime from the
  Strapi field config plus a schema function that loops over the config is a natural fit.
  Custom rules (legal age, vehicle year range) map to `validate()`. Strapi error messages
  map to `ValidationError.message`.
- ➕ Signal-native state (`valid()`, `touched()`, `errors()`) fits a signals-only wizard
  and avoids `toSignal` bridges.
- ➖ The model shape is only known at runtime, so typing degrades to `Record<string, …>`.
  The "typed validations" requirement then depends on a typed **config** contract, not on
  the form type.
- ➖ The skill's rules: no `null` values (use `''`/`0`), no `<select multiple>`, checkboxes
  bind only to booleans, and no `min/max/value` attributes on inputs. "Required number with
  initial value `0`" and empty date fields need a spike to confirm behaviour.
- ➖ It has been stable for only about 5 months. Reactive Forms (`FormRecord`) remain the
  proven path for dynamic forms and are still supported (`ReactiveFormsModule` is imported
  into a standalone component; we author no NgModules).

### Verdict: **ADOPT WITH ADJUSTMENTS**

**Reasons:** it is official, active, MIT, has no executable content, and is aligned with
Angular 22 (standalone, signals, control flow, Vitest, zoneless). Its main value is an
up-to-date Signal Forms and testing reference that our own skills do not provide and that
models tend to get wrong. The conflicts (C1–C6) can all be resolved with precedence and
explicit rules in `CLAUDE.md`, without editing vendored files.

**Required adjustments, if approved:**

1. Install only `angular-developer`, at project scope, and verify that the installed files
   match commit `97c663a` (diff). On mismatch, stop and re-evaluate.
2. Record the source, commit, upstream commit, license and copyright notice in
   `.claude/skills/THIRD_PARTY.md`.
3. Add the precedence rule to `CLAUDE.md` (CLAUDE.md > accepted ADRs > own skills >
   third-party) and the explicit overrides C1–C6.
4. Do not modify vendored files. Overrides live in `CLAUDE.md`, so a future update is a
   clean diff to re-evaluate.
5. Grant it to `angular-developer`, `test-engineer`, `code-reviewer` and `architect` (forms
   ADR only). Do not grant it to `spec-writer` or `strapi-developer`.

Decision: ADOPT WITH ADJUSTMENTS — approved by Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20.

content.content:
- **Root `/`**: country chooser listing the loaded countries as links ("Colombia", "Chile") to
  `/<code>/datos`. No detection from IP or browser locale.
- **Country list cannot be loaded** (Strapi down, timeout): the chooser and the unknown-country
  page show the same load error state as step 1 ("No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de
  nuevo." is form-specific, so the copy for this state is set by the spec; see *Spec impact*) with
  "Reintentar". The app never claims a country is unavailable when it simply could not check.
- **Switching country (US-01-Q-02)**: there is no in-page selector. Switching means opening the
  other country's address (from the chooser or by typing it). Entering a supported country's
  context whose code differs from the country held in the wizard state discards the stored state
  (mechanics in ADR-0003). Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not discard anything.

**Wizard routes and step guards (folded in from the spec §10 candidate)**

| Address | Route content | Guard | Story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | Country chooser page | — | US-01 |
| `/:country` | Parent route of the wizard; `canMatch: [supportedCountryGuard]` | country must be in `CountryStore` | US-01 |
| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/planes` | **No component** in US-01: `children: []` | `canActivate: [wizardStepGuard]` | US-01 registers it; US-02 attaches its page without changing address or guard (US-01-Q-27) |
| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |

- Step slugs are Spanish because they are user-visible (same status as the wizard chrome copy in
  US-01-Q-14); identifiers in code stay English.
### What is decided

**Store and storage key**

- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
  `values` follows spec §7.3 (`text` → trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option
  value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox` → boolean, empty optional → `null`). `plan` is added by
  US-02 (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
  lives only in the payment component's memory.
- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.

**When it is written**

- On every change of a step 1 value (the store writes synchronously after updating its signal), so
  a reload restores what the person typed, valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and
  on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16).

**When it is read**

- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.

# SPIKE-01: Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms for the Strapi-driven step 1 form

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Question | Which forms library fits a step 1 form built at runtime from the Strapi field configuration (`CLAUDE.md` §7, spec §10 item 2)? |
| Run by | frontend-developer subagent (Claude Opus 5.5), 2026-11-20 |
| Independent re-run | orchestrator, 2026-11-20: `@angular/core` and `@angular/forms` 22.3.0 installed, `ng build` OK, `ng test` 4 files, 38/38 passed |
| Written up by | architect subagent (Claude Opus 5.5), 2026-11-20 |
| Code | Branch `spike/01-forms`, commit `be9ae50`, folder `spikes/spike-01-forms/` (throwaway, **never merged**). GitHub: <https://github.com/FelipeSuarez25/multicountry-car-insurance/tree/spike/01-forms/spikes/spike-01-forms> |
| Decision informed | [ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-forms-library.md) (forms library) |

This document records facts only. The recommendation is in ADR-0004.

## Environment

| Item | Version or setting |
|---|---|
| Node | 24.22.1 |
| Scaffold | `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new spike-01-forms --directory spikes/spike-01-forms --skip-git --ssr=false --style=css --skip-install --defaults` |
| `@angular/core` / `forms` / `common` | 22.3.0 (checked in `node_modules`) |
| TypeScript | 6.0.3 |
| Vitest | 5.1.1 (through `ng test`, `@angular/build:unit-test`) |
| DOM | jsdom 31 (**no real browser**) |
| tsconfig | The CLI default has no `strict`; the spike adds `strict: true` and `resolveJsonModule: true`. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off. |
| Change detection | zoneless (CLI default) |

Environment notes: `ng build` hung silently on an interactive analytics prompt until
`NG_CLI_ANALYTICS=false CI=1` were set. `npm install` printed install-script warnings (esbuild,
lmdb, msgpackr-extract); build and tests were not affected. The spike `package.json` uses `^`
ranges, which is acceptable for a throwaway spike only (`CLAUDE.md` §4 applies to `frontend/`).

## Method

- One fixture JSON that follows the `dynamic-form-fields` contract v1 (57 lines), parsed at the
  boundary into typed `FieldConfig` objects.
- A **shared, library-agnostic core** (`src/app/core/`, 209 lines): pure functions with no
  Angular import except the `CLOCK` token (`InjectionToken<() => Date>`): `parseFieldConfigs`,
  `validateField(cfg, value, today)` (required, then empty-optional skip, then integer-only,
  then rules in configuration order; the first failing message wins), `hydrate`, `toOutput`,
  `parseIsoDate`, `ageOn`. `rutCheckDigit` is not implemented.
- Two adapters with the same inputs, output and test handles: Signal Forms
  (`signal-forms/dynamic-form-signal.*`, 111 lines) and Reactive Forms with `FormRecord`
  (`reactive-forms/dynamic-form-reactive.*`, 112 lines). Each field gets **one custom
  validator** that calls `validateField`. Built-in validators (`required()`, `min()`,
  `pattern()`, `Validators.*`) were not used.
- Tests (435 lines): `criteria.spec.ts` runs the same titled test against both adapters
  (`[signal-forms] (x)` / `[reactive-forms] (x)`); `core.spec.ts` covers the core once;
  `typing.spec.ts` covers compile-time behaviour; `library-facts.spec.ts` isolates library
  behaviour outside the shared criteria.
- API facts were read from the installed `@angular/forms` typings (`types/signals.d.ts`,
  `types/_structure-chunk.d.ts`) and compiled `fesm2022/*.mjs`.
- Sensitivity check: removing `focusBoundControl()` failed `[signal-forms] (i)`; removing
  `markAllAsTouched()` failed `[reactive-forms] (h)`. Both were restored.

## Results by criterion

| # | Criterion (source) | Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) | Reactive Forms (`FormRecord`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | Required number: empty vs `0` vs value; integer-only (`CLAUDE.md` §7, AC-05, AC-08) | **Works.** Model holds a **string** (`''` = empty); a string model on `<input type="number">` falls through to `element.value`. With a `number` model, clearing the input writes `null` and `2020.5` reaches the model, so integer-only is a validator, not a type. | **Works with a workaround.** `NumberValueAccessor` writes `number \| null` even into a `FormControl<string \| boolean>`; numeric `2020` was treated as empty until a `normalise()` step was added (validator input and output mapping). `nonNullable: true` does not stop the accessor writing `null`. Forcing `DefaultValueAccessor` was not tried. |
| b | Empty date, required vs optional; empty optional skips `minAge` (AC-06, AC-08) | **Works.** ISO string or `''`; string model on `type=date` falls through to `element.value`. | **Works**, same behaviour (`DefaultValueAccessor` handles `type=date` as a string). |
| c | Select required, nothing pre-selected (AC-07, BR-02) | **Works.** Model `''` plus placeholder `<option value="">`; `selectedIndex === 0`; options in `sortOrder`. | **Works**, same. |
| d | Legal age with an injectable clock (AC-06) | **Works.** `CLOCK` provided in TestBed; 18th birthday today valid, tomorrow invalid (today 2026-11-20). 29 February covered in `core.spec.ts`. | **Works**, same. |
| e | Typing with a runtime-built model (assessment: "typed validations") | Static model: precise keys and types. Runtime `Record<string, string \| boolean>`: any key compiles; an unknown key throws `TypeError` at runtime. The union **does not compile** against native controls, so two cast helpers were needed (see *Typing*). | Static `FormGroup`: precise. `FormRecord<FormControl<string \| boolean>>`: `controls[key]` typed (runtime `undefined` for an unknown key), `get(key)` nullable, `getRawValue()` → `Record<string, string \| boolean>`. `[formControl]` accepts the union **with no cast**. The runtime number value is `number \| null` despite the declared type. |
| f | Hydration from stored values (AC-04, AC-21) | **Works.** Model built from `hydrate(configs, stored)` before `form()`; `2020` → `'2020'`; pristine, untouched, no errors on entry; DOM shows input, select and checkbox values. A stored select value that is no longer an option keeps its model value, the select shows the placeholder, and the form is invalid. | **Works**, same results. |
| g | Drop stored values of keys no longer configured (AC-23) | **Works only because `hydrate()` filters by configuration before the model exists.** The model signal is the source of truth: an extra key written into it stays in `form().value()`. | **Works** through the same `hydrate()`. `FormGroup.setValue` with an extra key **throws**; `patchValue` ignores it. |
| h | When errors become visible (AC-10) | `submit()` marks the root as touched, which propagates to every field, so one condition `touched() && invalid()` covers blur and failed submit. Typing alone does not touch. After a failed submit: 3 alerts (birthDate, make, vehicleYear); optional fields stay quiet. | Needs an explicit `record.markAllAsTouched()` in the submit handler (removing it fails the test). `touched` is a plain property, not a signal; re-render worked because blur and `ngSubmit` are template listeners (zoneless). Same visible behaviour. |
| i | Focus on the first invalid field after a failed submit (AC-10) | **Works with a built-in API**: `onInvalid` → `root[key]().focusBoundControl()` on the first invalid field in `sortOrder`. `document.activeElement` checked across 3 consecutive attempts. | **No focus API on controls.** Workaround: `host.querySelector('#' + key).focus()` (id = key). Same result. |
| j | Output maps empty optional to `null` while the model stays non-null (§7.3, `CLAUDE.md` §7) | **Works.** Model `Record<string, string \| boolean>` (`''` / `false`); `toOutput()` produces `null`, integers and trimmed text; the model keeps what was typed (`'   '` stays in the model, output is `null`). | **Works** with the same `toOutput()`, after the `normalise()` workaround from (a). |

Totals: `[signal-forms]` a–j 11/11, `[reactive-forms]` a–j 11/11, core 8/8, typing 4/4, library
facts 4/4; 38/38 overall. `ng build` succeeds.

Checkbox note: an unchecked optional checkbox is output as `false`, not `null` (see unverified
item 5).

## Typing observations

- **Signal Forms, static model** (`signal({ vehicleYear: '', acceptsOffers: false })`):
  `f.vehicleYear().value()` is `string`; `f.nope` and `.value.set(2020)` are compile errors.
- **Signal Forms, runtime model** (`signal<Record<string, string | boolean>>`): `f['anything']`
  compiles as `FieldTree<string | boolean>`; an unknown key throws
  `TypeError: f.<key> is not a function` at runtime.
- **Signal Forms, binding the union in a template does not compile.** Captured `ng build` errors:
  text → `TS2322: Type 'WritableSignal<RawValue>' is not assignable to type '{ (): string; set: (v: string) => void; } | { (): number | null; set: (v: number | null) => void; }'`;
  checkbox → `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'boolean'`; number →
  `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | null'`; date →
  `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | Date | null'`.
  `FieldTree<string | boolean>` is not assignable to `FieldTree<string>`. Workaround: `str(key)`
  and `bool(key)` accessors doing `as unknown as FieldTree<string>` / `FieldTree<boolean>`
  (2 casts, chosen per field type in a static `@switch`).
- Value types accepted by native controls in Signal Forms: text → `string`; number →
  `string | number | null`; date → `string | number | Date | null`; checkbox → `boolean`.
- **Reactive Forms**, `FormRecord<FormControl<string | boolean>>`: `controls[key]` is
  `FormControl<string | boolean>` (no `undefined` because `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off);
  `get(key)` is nullable; `setValue(5)` is a compile error; `[formControl]` compiles with no cast.
- **Both:** the types describe the model, not what native controls write at runtime (`null` from
  a cleared number input).
- `form()` inside `computed()` throws `NG0602: effect() cannot be called from within a reactive
  context`, because `form()` creates an effect. The adapter wraps it in
  `untracked(() => form(...))`. `form()` also needs an injection context or `{ injector }`.
  Building a `FormRecord` inside `computed()` had no such issue.

## Gotchas found

1. A cleared `<input type="number">` writes `null` into a `number` model (Signal Forms) or a
   `nonNullable` control (Reactive Forms). Declared types do not protect against it.
2. Decimals reach the model in both libraries; integer-only must be a validator.
3. Reactive Forms: `NumberValueAccessor` overrides the declared control type, which produced a
   real functional bug in the spike (a valid year read as empty) until `normalise()` was added.
4. Signal Forms: the model is the source of truth and does not drop unknown keys; filtering by
   configuration must happen before the model is built.
5. Signal Forms: `form()` cannot be called inside `computed()` without `untracked`.
6. Reactive Forms: a failed submit does not touch the controls unless `markAllAsTouched()` is
   called; there is no control-level focus API.
7. Both: a configuration change while mounted rebuilds the form from `stored`; values typed since
   mount are lost unless the caller keeps `stored` current.
8. Tooling: `ng build` needs `NG_CLI_ANALYTICS=false CI=1` in a non-interactive shell.

## Not verified (open)

1. Everything ran in jsdom. Not checked in a real browser: focus and scroll behaviour, native
   `date` and `number` UI, `badInput` handling (`NativeInputParseError` exists in the source but
   was not exercised), mobile keyboards, screen reader announcement of `role="alert"`.
2. Blur was simulated with `new FocusEvent('blur')` and typing with `input`/`change` events; real
   event ordering was not covered.
3. Reactive Forms with a string model through `DefaultValueAccessor` (for example
   `type="text" inputmode="numeric"` or a custom accessor) was not tried.
4. `rutCheckDigit` was not implemented.
5. Output of an unchecked optional checkbox: `false` in the spike. Spec §7.3 says both
   "checkbox → boolean" and "empty optional field → `null`".
6. Whether step 1 can receive a different configuration while mounted (country switch) is a spec
   and routing question.
7. Async validators and `submit({ ignoreValidators })` were not exercised.
8. A dynamic `[type]` binding together with `[formField]` was avoided (static `@switch`
   branches), so it is unverified.
9. Bundle size, performance with many fields and SSR were not measured.
10. Error visibility is hand-built in both (`touched && invalid`); `provideSignalFormsConfig`
    (class and ARIA auto-binding) was not explored.
11. The vendored `signal-forms.md` forbids `null` in the model; the spike confirms that a non-null
    model with `null` only in the mapped output works, but also that `null` can still appear at
    runtime in a `number` model through native inputs (row a).
12. A third approach, binding native inputs to plain signals with no forms library, was not
    built. ADR-0004 weighs it from the shared-core evidence only.

  `string | number | null`; date → `string | number | Date | null`; checkbox → `boolean`.
